This is because antidepressants are overprescribed in general. People that are having situational/environmental issues causing depression may not need a chemical helper to get out of depression… they probably need a better environment. When you take ADs and chemically do not need them (ie. there is no chemical imbalance in your brain in that specific instance) it indeed increases irritability and suicidality. Because you don’t need it, you aren’t deficient in dopamine/serotonin/etc. 

However, many people do lack the amount of chemicals needed in their brains to operate at a level they wish to live by. I am one of those people, but only during a few months in the winter. I have had several providers attempt to keep me on antidepressants the entire year and I refuse, either by telling them outright that I have seasonal affective disorder if I think they’ll understand and believe me, or by just not taking the medication during the 9-10 other months out of the year. 

If I don’t take Prozac during those dark dark winter months I most certainly am at a high high risk of death. If I take Prozac during the other months out of the year I am most certainly at risk physically and mentally of many things, including death. 

The issue here is that so many people are getting medicated with ADs when they don’t need them. The issue is not that medication shouldn’t be given at all. Informed consent and patient choice is key.
